As part of a small, high-trust local team, you'll be the go-to person in the Lisbon office for day-to-day IT support - onboarding new hires, setting up hardware, keeping meeting rooms and workstations running - while also picking up real engineering work: automation scripting, CI/CD pipelines, and AWS infrastructure support alongside a distributed engineering team. You'll learn fast, work directly with senior engineers, and grow from executing well-defined tasks into owning small pieces of infrastructure independently. The Role at a Glance Be the local IT point of contact for the Lisbon office - onboarding, hardware, and everyday support. Learn and apply core SRE practices - scripting, CI/CD, and cloud infrastructure - under the guidance of senior engineers. Split your time between hands-on specialist work and hands-on engineering work; grow into more of the latter over time. Build a foundation in Linux, AWS, and automation that sets up a long-term engineering career path. What You'll Do & the Impact You'll Own Measured by growth and reliability, not tenure - within 6-12 months Own IT specialist duties for the Lisbon office: Handle new-hire onboarding end to end - hardware provisioning, account setup, workstation configuration, and welcome/orientation support - so new colleagues are productive from day one. Keep the local office running: Support workstations, conference rooms, and A/V equipment; manage local IT inventory and procurement; act as the first point of contact when something in the office isn't working. Provide day-to-day technical support: Troubleshoot common issues - login problems, device setup, network connectivity, basic Linux/Windows/macOS issues - and know when to escalate to the broader distributed team. Learn and contribute to automation: Write and maintain simple scripts and Ansible playbooks under guidance to reduce repetitive manual work; progressively take on larger pieces of automation as your skills grow. Support CI/CD and cloud infrastructure: Get hands-on with GitLab pipelines and AWS building blocks (IAM, EC2, basic networking) by shadowing and then assisting senior engineers on real infrastructure tasks. Build strong fundamentals: Develop working knowledge of Linux systems administration, version control, and cloud basics through real tickets and projects, not just documentation. Document and communicate clearly: Keep clear records of issues and fixes so recurring problems get solved once, not repeatedly; communicate status and blockers proactively to the wider (mostly remote) team. Scripting: Working knowledge of at least one scripting language (Python, Bash, or similar) and eagerness to write more of it. IT support mindset: Comfortable being hands-on with hardware and being the local face of IT - patient, clear communicator, good with people who arent technical. Cloud curiosity: Basic familiarity with a cloud platform (AWS preferred) and genuine interest in learning infrastructure and automation - formal production experience not required. Ownership and reliability: Able to work independently as the only (or one of very few) on-site technical resource, while staying closely connected to a distributed, remote-first team. Language: Fluent English (written and spoken); Portuguese is a plus for local vendor and office coordination. Education: Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Engineering, IT, or a related field; equivalent practical experience considered. Nice to Have Exposure to configuration management tools (Ansible, Puppet, Chef). Familiarity with Git and CI/CD concepts (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or similar). Coursework, certifications, or personal projects involving AWS (Cloud Practitioner or higher). Prior experience in a hardware/device support or IT helpdesk role.
